requirement_text.REQ-358: DECISION BEING REVISITED, NAMED EXPLICITLY PER CORE-DIRECTIVES' "don't silently re-decide a settled decision" rule. Decision 0004 ("What is explicitly NOT reproduced") deferred R-Co's BO-*/PRODUCT-OWNER persona layer "to when S7 actually starts and there is a concrete scenario corpus to validate against." .claude/agents/uat-runner.md's own "Note on scope" restates the same condition. REQ-210 (S7's closing requirement, done) confirmed both preconditions are now met: S7 is done, and a real scenario corpus exists (11 tenant scenarios across 3 companies, 18 platform scenarios, test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/). This requirement and REQ-359..362 are the deferred work whose trigger condition has now fired — not a reopening of the decision's reasoning, which remains correct as stated for the period before this precondition held. REVIEWER should confirm this reading before this requirement's dependents proceed rather than treat it as implicitly pre-approved. . WHY THIS REQUIREMENT IS SEPARATE FROM REQ-359/360. Both the new BA-role requirement (REQ-359) and the PRODUCT-OWNER-port requirement (REQ-361) need scenario files that can express conditional branching (e.g. "if role=PLATFORM_ADMIN assert dashboard A, elif role=<tenant-role> assert dashboard B, else assert login form") and need UAT-RUNNER able to target a specific environment (base URL + credential source) rather than "a real running instance" left generic. Neither of those two role/agent requirements should each re-derive this schema/runner change independently — it is shared, load-bearing infrastructure for both, so it is its own requirement, sized and landed first. . SCOPE. 1. Extend the UAT scenario YAML schema (the format test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/**/*.yaml already uses) with: (a) a `scope` field distinguishing `platform` from a tenant-vertical identifier (adapt R-Co's uat-scenario-schema-v1.1-addendum.md's `company_id` field and its documented classification rule — "if a business user... would notice the behaviour, the scenario keeps its [tenant] scope... use `platform` only when the actor is the platform operator or the platform itself" — to Letflow's own tenant model, which has no fixed set of named tenant companies the way R-Co's SwiftRoute/Vortex/Meridian did; the field's value should be an open tenant-vertical/solution-pack identifier, not a closed enum of three); (b) a branching construct at the step level (a `when:`/condition key gating which of several named sub-paths of steps/expected_outcomes apply, keyed on a runtime-observable fact such as the authenticated user's role) sufficient to express the login-routing example above without inventing a general-purpose scripting language — keep the construct as narrow as the actual need, per this project's own anti-over-engineering directive. 2. Extend UAT-RUNNER (docs/agents/workflows/WF-05_uat_run.md and .claude/agents/uat-runner.md) to accept an explicit environment target: a base URL (e.g. https://qa.bizdala.com) and a named credential source (e.g. ai-dala-infra/scripts/qa-login.sh's seeded users) rather than assuming "whatever instance is reachable." Update .claude/agents/uat-runner.md's "Note on scope" section to remove the now-stale "your report is read directly by RELEASE-VALIDATOR, not by a persona layer" sentence and replace it with a pointer to REQ-361's PRODUCT-OWNER-equivalent role once that requirement lands (do not forward-reference an agent that does not exist yet as though it already does — word this as "as of REQ-361" per this project's own citation discipline). 3. Update WF-05_uat_run.md's step sequence to reflect the branching evaluation and environment-target steps this adds — do not leave the workflow doc silently out of sync with the runner's actual new behaviour. NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no new agent role (REQ-359/361), no actual login-routing scenario authored (REQ-360 or wherever the first platform-scope scenario using this schema lands — flag as a fast-follow if not otherwise covered), no visual-regression mechanism (REQ-362).

task.description:
Design (no implementation code — signatures/shapes/docs structure only) the three pieces of REQ-358's SCOPE section above, all three of which this run must ship together:

1. THE SCHEMA EXTENSION. Read one real existing scenario file (test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/meridian/loan-origination-below-threshold.yaml, listed in artifacts_in) to see the current shape (company_id, steps[], expected_outcomes[] as documented there). Design: (a) a `scope:` field (values: `platform`, or an open tenant-vertical identifier string — NOT a closed enum of company names; document the classification rule from the requirement text: 'if a business user would notice the behaviour, the scenario keeps its tenant scope; use platform only when the actor is the platform operator or the platform itself'). Decide and document explicitly how `scope:` relates to the existing `company_id:` field (e.g. does `scope` supersede it, coexist with it as a broader category, or is `company_id` folded into being one instance of a tenant-vertical `scope` value?) — this is exactly the kind of design decision this step exists to make explicit rather than leaving implicit. (b) A step-level branching construct: a `when:`/condition key on a step (or on a named group of steps) that gates which of several named sub-paths of steps/expected_outcomes apply, keyed on a runtime-observable fact (e.g. `role`). Design it narrow: state the exact YAML shape (keys, allowed operators — e.g. equality only, or equality+in-list — and how UAT-RUNNER is meant to read/evaluate it procedurally, since UAT-RUNNER is a Claude subagent following markdown instructions, not an Elixir interpreter) sufficient to express: role=PLATFORM_ADMIN -> assert dashboard A; role=<tenant-role> -> assert dashboard B; else (unauthenticated) -> assert login form. Do NOT design a general-purpose scripting/expression language — this must be answerable by a weak model reading the instructions procedurally. (c) Confirm and document backward compatibility explicitly: every field this design adds must be OPTIONAL with a defined default (e.g. absent `scope:` defaults to reading `company_id:` as today), so all 29 existing scenario files (11 tenant + 18 platform) parse unchanged under the new schema with unchanged behavior — this is REQ-358's AC1. Document the doc's home: docs/agents/uat-scenario-schema.md (new file — there is no existing 'schema doc' home under docs/agents/ today; confirm this by checking, and if a better home already exists, use it and say why in the design doc's Open Questions instead of silently picking one).

2. THE SCHEMA-VALIDATION MIX TASK (REQ-358 AC2 — this is real Elixir application-executable surface, not a docs-only requirement: 'a schema-validation check matching the existing dry-run/schema-gate pattern this project already uses elsewhere for structured YAML, e.g. mix letflow.check's requirements-registration check'). Read lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_requirements_registration.ex (artifacts_in) as the precedent pattern to follow structurally (a `mix letflow.check_*` task, wired into mix.exs's `letflow.check` alias, that walks a set of structured files, parses each, and fails loudly with a specific file+reason on a malformed one). Design a new mix task, working name `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_uat_scenario_schema.ex`, that: walks test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/**/*.yaml, parses each against this design's schema (required fields, `scope`'s classification rule enforceable mechanically only to the extent it is mechanical — e.g. 'scope must be present-or-defaulted and be a non-empty string' is mechanical; 'is this the right classification for this scenario' is not, and should not be faked as a mechanical check), and exits non-zero with a clear per-file error on a malformed file. Specify the exact function signatures/module shape (@spec-style), the exact error message shape, and how it is wired into mix.exs's `aliases()/letflow.check` list (a concrete diff-shaped instruction, not code). This task is the AC2 acceptance-criteria vehicle: 'a passing example is quoted' and 'rejects a malformed scope/branching scenario file with a clear error' both come from running this task for real in Step 2a.

3. UAT-RUNNER + WF-05 ENVIRONMENT-TARGET AND BRANCHING-EVALUATION UPDATES. Both .claude/agents/uat-runner.md and docs/agents/workflows/WF-05_uat_run.md are markdown instruction files for a Claude subagent, not Elixir modules — design here means: specify exactly what new input UAT-RUNNER's dispatch handoff must carry (a base URL and a named credential source, per the requirement text's ai-dala-infra/scripts/qa-login.sh example — READ .claude/agents/uat-runner.md's own current 'Note on scope' section, quoted in the requirement text and in artifacts_in, so your design's replacement wording is exact, not paraphrased), and specify the exact procedural steps UAT-RUNNER must follow to evaluate a `when:` branch against an actual authenticated session's role during a real run. Write these as literal proposed markdown edits (the new/replacement prose) in the design doc's own section for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and ELIXIR-DEV to apply verbatim, not as a vague description of intent.

Write the design artefact(s) to lib/letflow/design/req358-uat-scope-branching-env.md per Step 1's standard procedure (WF-02_requirement_implementation.md, already read). List every open question explicitly rather than silently resolving it (e.g. the company_id/scope relationship above, or the exact branch-condition operator set, if you're genuinely unsure which the requirement intends).

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed this design (handoffs/WF02-REQ358-20260916/step-01b-design-gate.json). Finding: the design doc's §0 premise 'Project has no YAML-parsing dependency in mix.exs today' is factually wrong — mix.exs already declares `{:yaml_elixir, "~> 2.11", only: :test}`, already used by lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex and several test-support/fixture modules. OQ-1 ("which YAML-parsing dependency to add") is therefore not a genuine open question needing new REVIEWER library sign-off — it is a concrete, resolvable decision: reuse yaml_elixir. FIX REQUIRED: (a) update the design doc to name yaml_elixir as the parsing library for the new mix task, remove OQ-1 as an open question (or narrow it to something genuinely unresolved, if anything remains); (b) yaml_elixir is currently scoped `only: :test` in mix.exs's deps() — but this design wires the new check into `letflow.check`'s alias list, which per this project's own mix.exs `preferred_envs: ["letflow.check": :test]` (grep it) already runs in the :test env, so confirm explicitly in the design doc whether the existing `only: :test` scoping is therefore already sufficient (most likely, given the alias's declared preferred_envs) or whether it genuinely needs widening — state the concrete conclusion, not another deferred question. Do not repeat the original design otherwise; this is a targeted addendum to the existing doc, not a rewrite. On completion, flip status to COMPLETED/FAILED as normal (not 'claim by setting status to IN_PROGRESS' — the handoff is already claimed).
acceptance_criteria: Every phrase of REQ-358's four acceptance criteria (quoted in context.requirement_text above) maps to a concrete, explicit design element in lib/letflow/design/req358-uat-scope-branching-env.md — no criterion left to be improvised by ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER later

The schema extension's backward-compatibility story is stated as a concrete mechanism (default values, optional fields), not an assertion — sufficient for ELIXIR-DEV to verify AC1 by actually re-running UAT-RUNNER against an existing unmodified scenario file and quoting its unchanged disposition

The mix task design specifies exact module name, public function signature(s), the mix.exs aliases() wiring point, and the exact shape of a rejection error message — no implementation code (.ex bodies) present in the design doc

The branching construct is proven sufficient on paper for the login-routing example (role=PLATFORM_ADMIN / role=<tenant-role> / unauthenticated, three distinct outcomes) by writing out, in the design doc, exactly what a throwaway scenario fixture using it would look like for that example — this is the design ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER will turn into REQ-358's own throwaway validation fixture in Step 2/3, not committed permanent scope

UAT-RUNNER's and WF-05's proposed replacement prose (environment-target input, branch-evaluation procedure, and the 'Note on scope' section's stale-sentence replacement pointing at 'as of REQ-361') is written out verbatim in the design doc, ready to apply
Open questions section lists anything not obvious from the requirement text rather than silently guessing

result.summary: Designed all three REQ-358 pieces in lib/letflow/design/req358-uat-scope-branching-env.md: (1) an optional `scope:` field coexisting with the existing `company_id:` field, with a documented default-derivation rule for backward compatibility (absent `scope` reads from `company_id`: 'platform' literal or the company name itself), plus a narrow step-level `branches:`/`when:` construct (fact/op/value with only `eq`/`in`/`else`, no expression language) proven sufficient on paper via a throwaway login-routing fixture (PLATFORM_ADMIN / tenant role / unauthenticated, three distinct outcomes); (2) `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_uat_scenario_schema.ex` designed structurally after letflow.check_requirements_registration.ex (run/1, check_file/1, check_scenario/2, render/1 signatures; SCHEMA-1..6 mechanical rules; exact [rule] file: message error shape; mix.exs aliases() wiring diff placed after letflow.check_issue_refs); (3) verbatim replacement/new-section markdown for .claude/agents/uat-runner.md (Environment target section, Evaluating a `when:` branch section, Note-on-scope replacement citing 'as of REQ-361') and docs/agents/workflows/WF-05_uat_run.md (Step 1/Step 2-3 additions, Deferred-personas sentence replacement). 5 open questions flagged explicitly (YAML-dependency choice needing REVIEWER sign-off per project precedent, per-step/per-outcome validation depth inside branches, fact vocabulary beyond `role`, ai-dala-infra credential_source invocation mechanism (outside this repo, not in artifacts_in), branch-level preconditions merge-vs-replace semantics) rather than silently resolved.
